payload.claim: No test in tests/test_mutant_command.py ever builds a spec file that declares an inline `mutant:` key, so the `refuse_inline_mutants(spec)` call on this line is never exercised through `write_mutants`. `refuse_inline_mutants` itself is already unit-tested in tests/test_intake.py, but that only proves the function works in isolation, not that `saffron mutant` actually invokes it. Deleting this line (and its now-unused import) would leave every test in the new file green, since `write_mutants` would still exit 0 on every spec the test suite constructs and no refusal test's spec declares `mutant:` inline. The Problem section and step 1 of the Build both require the command to refuse such a spec, mirroring `run_task`, but the acceptance-criteria tests never check it.
